newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Exiled prince faces jail if returns - Cambodian PM.
newsitem.headline: Exiled prince faces jail if returns - Cambodian PM.

text.p: A Cambodian prince exiled more than two years ago for his role in a failed coup will be arrested if he returns home without a pardon, co-Premier Hun Sen said on Wednesday.

Prince Norodom Chakrapong, son of King Norodom Sihanouk, told the Phnom Penh Post in recent interviews at his Paris home that he wanted to return home from exile but doubted that his former political ally Hun Sen would agree.
Chakrapong was exiled after a failed coup bid in July 1994 and later convicted in absentia by a military tribunal and sentenced to 20 years imprisonment.

"Chakrapong's case is the same as Sirivudh's case, if there is an amnesty from the king there is no problem," Hun Sen told reporters, adding: "If he comes without the king's amnesty, police will meet him at the airport and take him to T3 prison."
He said the sentence handed down on his former colleague in the coalition government's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) was still in effect.
Prince Norodom Sirivudh, half-brother of the king and a former foreign minister, was exiled to France in December 1995 after he was detained for allegedly plotting to assassinate Hun Sen.
A court later sentenced him to 10 years on charges connected to the alleged plot, which he has denied.
The king, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and CPP president Chea Sim are all believed to favour granting amnesties to the princes and other political exiles and prisoners.
A royal amnesty was granted to former top Khmer Rouge cadre Ieng Sary at the request of the two premiers.

The king pardoned him from a 1979 death sentence handed down in absentia for his role in the deaths of more than one million people during the 1975-79 Khmer Rouge rule. The move paved the way for thousands of rebels to defect.
Sihanouk has said he will not grant amnesties without Hun Sen approval, while the second prime minister warned in December that he would attack any plane bringing Sirivudh back to Cambodia.
He later said the prince could return with an amnesty.
